subject.title: Feature: Surface cron job name / session label in /status and statusline

question: Should maintainers close/supersede the conflicting fork PR and sponsor a narrow upstream status-label fix, or ask that PR author to rebase and prove the current branch?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the issue has product-decision/no-new-fix-pr signals and an open linked PR that is conflicting and based on a previously closed unmerged attempt.

options.title: Close/supersede and sponsor a narrow fix
options.body: Keep this issue canonical, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and land a focused owner-reviewed fix with terminal-safe label rendering.

options.title: Ask for a PR rebase and proof
options.body: Keep this issue open while asking the fork PR author to rebase, add sanitization, and provide real behavior proof.

options.title: Defer to broader attribution design
options.body: Leave this issue open as product-direction input for the broader status/usage attribution work, accepting raw keys in CLI/TUI status for now.

recommendation.title: Close/supersede and sponsor a narrow fix
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical, close or supersede the conflicting fork PR, and land a focused owner-reviewed fix with terminal-safe label rendering.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent TUI session lifecycle and cron/session-targeting history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the cross-surface product choice.
